clue.text: Marvellous article about one British socialist

indicators.note: used loosely here to put the article beside one, so the two pieces sit side by side

explanation.surface: A wonderful newspaper piece about a single British left-winger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' is a loose positional link here: the article attaches to one rather than wrapping it. The Fabian Society is a long-standing British socialist group.
explanation.definitionFit: A Fabian is a member of the Fabian Society, a gradualist socialist organisation founded in London.

clue.text: Considered pieces of advice for writers?

parts.note: felt as in thought or believed

explanation.surface: Thoughtful hints aimed at authors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writers' looks like authors, but the question mark signals things that write: pens.
explanation.definitionFit: Felt tips are pens with a felt nib, so they are literally implements that write.

clue.text: Boy on Caribbean island mountain

parts.note: Nevis is an island in St Kitts and Nevis

explanation.surface: A lad is standing on a hill on a West Indian island.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Nevis, in the Scottish Highlands, is the highest peak in Britain.

clue.text: A component in pieces

explanation.surface: A single component lying broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taken apart is separated into its pieces, so the adverb matches 'in pieces'.

clue.text: Account, by media abroad, about scholar

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or scattered, so these letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: c is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A financial report by the foreign press concerning a university lecturer.
explanation.definitionFit: An academic is a university teacher or researcher, a scholar by profession.

clue.text: Seat cushion Gale mended with bit of embroidery

indicators.note: something mended has been reworked, so these letters are put back in a new order
a bit of a word is just one of its letters, here its opening one

explanation.surface: A woman named Gale repairs a seat cushion with a little needlework.
explanation.walkthrough: Gale reads as a seamstress's name; it is just four letters for the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaise longue is a long upholstered sofa with a backrest at one end, a kind of seat.

clue.text: The cod, once processed, is taken across road leading right out of Dutch port

indicators.note: to be taken across something is to span it, so the outer letters straddle the inner ones
fish that has been processed has been cut up and rearranged, so the letters are reordered
one piece leading another means it goes in front of it

explanation.surface: Processed cod is carted along a road heading out of a harbour in the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled fish letters wrap around road followed by right.
explanation.definitionFit: Dordrecht is an old river port city in the Dutch province of South Holland.

clue.text: Second girl guarding queen in place of worship

parts.note: mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: guarding something means standing around it, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: Q is the chess abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A second girl protects the queen in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosque is a Muslim building for prayer, a place of worship.

clue.text: Bright Catholic bar

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Catholic
a lever is a rigid bar used to pry

explanation.surface: An intelligent Catholic, or a cheerful Catholic pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright in the sense of intelligent is a synonym of clever.

clue.text: Put down in front of gold carriage

parts.note: to land is to put down, as of a plane
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Setting something down before a golden coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In front of' places the first piece before the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding top.

clue.text: A pass from the wing intercepted by the French in game

indicators.note: something intercepted is caught in the middle, so one word is wrapped by the other

parts.note: a cross is a pass from the wing in football, preceded by A

explanation.surface: A wide pass is cut out by the French team in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team sport played with netted sticks, a game.

clue.text: Pompous type with press, dithers terribly

parts.note: to stuff is to press or cram

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A self-important figure faced with reporters hesitates badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuffed shirt is an idiom for a pompous, stiffly formal person.

clue.text: Article on conditions in America?

parts.note: states are conditions, as in a state of repair

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about conditions in the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In America' looks like part of the surface; America alone, with its question mark, is the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The States is an informal name for the United States of America.

clue.text: A way to drive off foremost of enemies

parts.note: to rout an enemy is to drive it off in defeat

indicators.note: the foremost part of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A method for chasing away the leading foes.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is a road or path taken, a way from one place to another.

clue.text: The most important position that the kings of beasts take?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the top spot of honour

definitions.text: that the kings of beasts take?
definitions.meaning: second, playful meaning: lions live in a pride, so their spot is the pride's place

explanation.walkthrough: Lions are the kings of beasts and a group of lions is a pride, so the place a pride takes reads literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Pride of place is an idiom for the most prominent or honoured position.

clue.text: HM meeting awfully intense girl

parts.note: Her Majesty is the Queen, Elizabeth Regina

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the letters come out in a disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: The Queen meets an extremely earnest young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: HM is Her Majesty; ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernestine is a female given name, so it fits a girl by example.

clue.text: After whip is raised, I become disinclined to speak

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising a word lifts it bottom to top, so it reads backwards

parts.note: to turn is to become, as in turn sour

explanation.surface: Once the lash is lifted, I fall silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Taciturn describes someone reserved who says very little.

clue.text: Drink always kept in container on top of escritoire

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece on another sits above it, so it comes first
kept in means held inside, so one word sits within the other
in a down entry the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A drink is permanently stored in a box resting on a writing desk.
explanation.walkthrough: An escritoire is a writing desk.
explanation.definitionFit: A beverage is any drink other than water.

clue.text: Place associated with bites and bytes?

definitions.text: Place associated with bites and bytes?

parts.words: Place associated with bites and bytes?
parts.note: surface reading: somewhere linked to eating and computing
setter's reading: bites of food and bytes of data, so a café where you eat while online

explanation.walkthrough: The near-homophones bites and bytes point to snacks and computer data in the same venue.
explanation.definitionFit: An internet café serves food and drink while renting computer access, so both kinds of byte are on offer.

clue.text: Chart, old, discovered in Cadiz, surprisingly

indicators.note: something discovered in a place is found inside it, so one letter sits within the rest
surprisingly suggests an unexpected result, so the letters come out in an unforeseen order

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An ancient map turns up unexpectedly in the Spanish city of Cadiz.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac is the astrological chart of twelve signs used in horoscopes.

clue.text: Held in awe, a ponderous missile perhaps

indicators.note: held in means contained within, so the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: runs across the words, ignoring the comma

explanation.surface: A heavy missile is regarded with fear and wonder.
explanation.definitionFit: A missile is one example of a weapon, as 'perhaps' signals.

clue.text: US athlete improved in very good round

indicators.note: turning something round makes it face the other way, so the combined letters run backwards
in means placed inside, so one word goes within the other

explanation.surface: An American sprinter got better during a very good lap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like a lap of the track or the letter O, but it reverses the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Jesse Owens was the American sprinter who won four gold medals at the 1936 Olympics.

clue.text: Wise and smart, brief comment heard on the news?

definitions.text: brief comment heard on the news?

parts.note: to smart is to sting, as a bite does

explanation.surface: A shrewd, witty remark quoted on the bulletin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' reads as clever, but here it is the verb to sting.
explanation.definitionFit: A soundbite is a short extract of speech broadcast in news programmes.

clue.text: Live in little valley round bottom of Skiddaw

indicators.note: round means encircling, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: a dell is a small wooded valley

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Residing in a small valley near the foot of a Lake District mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: Skiddaw is a mountain in England's Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to reside somewhere, so it matches the verb live.

clue.text: Understood one must have allowed member inside

indicators.note: inside means within, so the member goes into the middle of the other letters

explanation.surface: It's taken as read that someone admitted a member.
explanation.definitionFit: Implicit means implied rather than stated, i.e. tacitly understood.

clue.text: Monster captured by armed US agent

indicators.note: captured by means held within, so the letters are inside the following words

explanation.surface: A beast is caught by an armed American operative.
explanation.definitionFit: Medusa is the snake-haired Gorgon of Greek myth, a monster whose gaze turned people to stone.

clue.text: Small pieces of paper often circulated in court by one

indicators.note: by means next to, so the last piece follows on
in means placed inside, so the shuffled letters go within the other piece
circulated means passed around, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Scraps of paper are frequently passed around a courtroom by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Confetti is tiny paper pieces thrown at weddings and celebrations.

clue.text: Batting stroke, good cut

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
to lance is to cut open, as a boil

explanation.surface: A neat stroke with the bat, a good cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like another cricket stroke, but it is the verb to lance. In cricket, a glance is a shot deflecting the ball fine off the bat face.
explanation.definitionFit: A glance, or leg glance, is a cricket shot that angles the ball away behind the batsman.
